DEFINITION · qeva:1:expression@1

Expression

An expression is a finite arrangement of symbols built by explicit formation rules.

editorialfoundations · language
Trace this conceptSearch connections

PLAIN

The idea

An expression is a finite arrangement of symbols built by explicit formation rules.

EXACT

The compact statement

Given an alphabet Σ and a grammar G, Expr(G) is the least class containing the atomic expressions and closed under the constructors declared by G.

Example

If x and y are terms and + is binary, +(x,y) may be a well-formed term.

Boundary / caveat

Well-formedness is syntax; it does not guarantee meaning or truth.

Assumptions

  • The declared formal language context is fixed.
